title: At the café
intro: You sit down in a café in Amman and order tea and a pastry. Useful phrases: مِنْ فَضْلِكَ (please, to a man), أُرِيدُ (I want) and كَمْ؟ (how much?).

dialogue.title: Tea for two
dialogue.culture: Tea is usually served sweet and often with fresh mint (نَعْنَاع). If you don't want sugar, say بِدُونِ سُكَّر.

lines.ar: مَسَاءُ الْخَيْر! أَهْلًا وَسَهْلًا. مَاذَا تُرِيدُ؟
lines.en: Good evening! Welcome. What would you like?

lines.ar: مَسَاءُ النُّور! أُرِيدُ شَايًا، مِنْ فَضْلِكَ.
lines.en: Good evening! I would like a tea, please.

lines.ar: شَاي بِالنَّعْنَاع أَوْ شَاي عَادِيّ؟
lines.en: Tea with mint, or ordinary tea?

lines.ar: بِالنَّعْنَاع، مِنْ فَضْلِكَ، وَبِدُونِ سُكَّر.
lines.en: With mint, please, and without sugar.

lines.ar: حَاضِر! هَلْ تُرِيدُ شَيْئًا آخَر؟ عِنْدَنَا كَعْك طَازَج.
lines.en: Certainly! Would you like anything else? We have fresh cake.

lines.ar: نَعَم، قِطْعَة كَعْك وَاحِدَة، مِنْ فَضْلِكَ.
lines.en: Yes, one piece of cake, please.

lines.ar: تَفَضَّلْ، الشَّاي وَالْكَعْك. بِالْهَنَاء وَالشِّفَاء!
lines.en: Here you are, the tea and the cake. Enjoy your meal!

lines.ar: شُكْرًا! الشَّاي لَذِيذ جِدًّا.
lines.en: Thank you! The tea is really very delicious.

lines.ar: مِنْ فَضْلِكَ، الْحِسَاب. كَمِ الْحِسَاب؟
lines.en: Excuse me, the bill please. How much is the bill?

lines.ar: ثَلَاثَة دَنَانِير، مِنْ فَضْلِكَ. شُكْرًا وَمَعَ السَّلَامَة!
lines.en: Three dinars, please. Thank you, and goodbye!

mistakes.why: After a verb the object takes the -an ending in careful MSA; in everyday speech people often drop it.
-ka for a man, -ki for a woman.

quiz.prompt: How do you say 'please' to a man?
What does Daniel not want in his tea?
What does this mean?

title: Taking a taxi
intro: You take a taxi in Cairo to the Egyptian Museum. Useful phrases: إِلَى (to), يَمِين (right), يَسَار (left) and هُنَا (here).

dialogue.title: To the museum
dialogue.culture: Agree on the fare before you set off, or check that the meter (الْعَدَّاد) is switched on.

lines.ar: مَرْحَبًا! إِلَى الْمَتْحَف الْمِصْرِيّ، مِنْ فَضْلِكَ.
lines.en: Hello! To the Egyptian Museum, please.

lines.ar: أَهْلًا! الْمَتْحَف قَرِيب، فِي مَيْدَانِ التَّحْرِير.
lines.en: Hi! The museum is close, on Tahrir Square.

lines.ar: كَمِ الْأُجْرَة إِلَى الْمَتْحَف، مِنْ فَضْلِكَ؟
lines.en: How much is the fare to the museum, please?

lines.ar: خَمْسُونَ جُنَيْهًا. الطَّرِيق مُزْدَحِم الْيَوْم.
lines.en: Fifty pounds. The road is very crowded today.

lines.ar: خَمْسُونَ كَثِير! أَرْبَعُونَ، مِنْ فَضْلِكَ؟
lines.en: Fifty is a lot! How about forty, please?

lines.ar: طَيِّب، أَرْبَعُونَ. تَفَضَّلِي!
lines.en: OK, forty then. Please get in!

lines.ar: هَلْ أَذْهَبُ يَمِينًا هُنَا أَوْ يَسَارًا؟
lines.en: Do I go right here, or left?

lines.ar: يَمِينًا، ثُمَّ إِلَى الْأَمَام، مِنْ فَضْلِكَ.
lines.en: Right, and then straight ahead, please.

lines.ar: هٰذَا هُوَ الْمَتْحَف الْمِصْرِيّ. وَصَلْنَا!
lines.en: This is the Egyptian Museum. We have arrived!

lines.ar: شُكْرًا جَزِيلًا! تَفَضَّلْ، أَرْبَعُونَ جُنَيْهًا. مَعَ السَّلَامَة!
lines.en: Thank you very much! Here you are, forty pounds. Goodbye!

mistakes.why: To say 'go right', the word takes the -an ending: yamīnan.

quiz.prompt: Where does Layla want to go?
What fare do they agree on?
What does this mean?

title: Morning with a host family
intro: It is your first morning with an Egyptian host family, and your host, Mrs Huda, asks about your routine. Useful phrases: مَتَى تَسْتَيْقِظُ؟ (when do you wake up?), أَشْرَبُ (I drink) and لَا آكُلُ كَثِيرًا (I don't eat much).

dialogue.title: Coffee, and no excuses
dialogue.culture: In Egypt it is polite to call an older woman خَالَة (aunt) and an older man عَمّ (uncle), even when you are not related. A host will nearly always insist that you eat breakfast.

lines.ar: صَبَاحُ الْخَيْر يَا دَانْيَال! كَيْفَ حَالُكَ الْيَوْم؟
lines.en: Good morning, Daniel! How are you today?

lines.ar: صَبَاحُ النُّور يَا خَالَة هُدَى! أَنَا بِخَيْر، الْحَمْدُ لِلّٰه.
lines.en: Good morning, Auntie Huda! I am fine, thank God.
segs: aunt (polite address for an older woman)

lines.ar: مَتَى تَسْتَيْقِظُ عَادَةً؟ أَنَا أَسْتَيْقِظُ فِي السَّاعَة السَّادِسَة.
lines.en: When do you usually wake up? I wake up at six o'clock.

lines.ar: أَسْتَيْقِظُ فِي السَّاعَة السَّادِسَة وَالنِّصْف، ثُمَّ أَغْسِلُ وَجْهِي.
lines.en: I wake up at half past six, then I wash my face.

lines.ar: وَمَاذَا تَشْرَبُ فِي الصَّبَاح؟ شَاي أَوْ قَهْوَة؟
lines.en: And what do you drink in the morning? Tea or coffee?

lines.ar: أَشْرَبُ الْقَهْوَة، مِنْ فَضْلِكِ، بِدُونِ سُكَّر.
lines.en: I drink coffee, please, without sugar.

lines.ar: حَاضِر. وَالْفُطُور؟ عِنْدِي فُول وَخُبْز وَبَيْض.
lines.en: Right away. And breakfast? I have beans, bread and eggs.

lines.ar: شُكْرًا يَا خَالَة، لٰكِنْ أَنَا لَا آكُلُ كَثِيرًا فِي الصَّبَاح.
lines.en: Thank you, Auntie, but I don't eat much in the morning.
segs: aunt (polite address for an older woman)

lines.ar: لَا، لَا! الْفُطُور مُهِمّ. كُلْ قَلِيلًا عَلَى الْأَقَلّ!
lines.en: No, no! Breakfast is important. At least eat a little!

lines.ar: حَاضِر! وَمَتَى يَخْرُجُ اِبْنُكِ حَسَن إِلَى الْمَدْرَسَة؟
lines.en: All right! And when does your son Hassan leave for school?

lines.ar: حَسَن يَخْرُجُ فِي السَّاعَة السَّابِعَة وَالنِّصْف، وَيَذْهَبُ بِالْحَافِلَة.
lines.en: Hassan leaves at half past seven, and he goes by bus.

lines.ar: وَأَنَا أَخْرُجُ فِي السَّاعَة الثَّامِنَة، لِأَنَّ الدَّرْس فِي السَّاعَة التَّاسِعَة.
lines.en: And I leave at eight o'clock, because the lesson is at nine.

lines.ar: مُمْتَاز. تَفَضَّلْ، الْقَهْوَة جَاهِزَة. صَبَاح جَمِيل يَا دَانْيَال!
lines.en: Excellent. Here you are, the coffee is ready. Have a lovely morning, Daniel!

mistakes.why: Speaking to a woman, the verb ends in -īna: tastayqiẓīna.
lā goes directly before the verb, not before the pronoun.

quiz.prompt: When does Daniel wake up?
What does Daniel drink in the morning?
What does this mean?
options: I don't eat much in the morning.
I eat a lot in the morning.
I don't drink coffee in the morning.

quiz.prompt: How do you politely address an older woman in Egypt?

title: Booking an appointment
intro: You go to the school office to book an appointment with the director. Useful phrases: أُرِيدُ مَوْعِدًا (I would like an appointment), هَلْ … مُمْكِن؟ (is … possible?), and the days and times from this week.

dialogue.title: Wednesday at quarter to three
dialogue.culture: When you book a time, repeat the day and the hour back to the other person. It avoids mix-ups between similar words such as الْخَمِيس (Thursday) and الْخَامِسَة (five o'clock).

lines.ar: صَبَاحُ الْخَيْر، هٰذَا مَكْتَبُ الْمَدْرَسَة. كَيْفَ أُسَاعِدُكَ؟
lines.en: Good morning, this is the school office. How can I help you?

lines.ar: صَبَاحُ النُّور. أَنَا دَانْيَال، طَالِب فِي صَفِّ الْأُسْتَاذ كَرِيم. أُرِيدُ مَوْعِدًا مَعَ الْمُدِير.
lines.en: Good morning. I am Daniel, a student in Mr Karim's class. I would like an appointment with the director.

lines.ar: طَبْعًا. هَلْ يَوْمُ الثُّلَاثَاء مُمْكِن، فِي السَّاعَة الْعَاشِرَة؟
lines.en: Of course. Is Tuesday possible, at ten o'clock?

lines.ar: آسِف، يَوْمَ الثُّلَاثَاء فِي السَّاعَة الْعَاشِرَة عِنْدِي دَرْس.
lines.en: Sorry, on Tuesday at ten o'clock I have a lesson.

lines.ar: لَا مُشْكِلَة. وَيَوْمَ الْأَرْبِعَاء؟ الْمُدِير هُنَا مِنَ السَّاعَة الْوَاحِدَة إِلَى السَّاعَة الرَّابِعَة.
lines.en: No problem. And on Wednesday? The director is here from one o'clock to four o'clock.

lines.ar: الْأَرْبِعَاء مُمْتَاز. هَلِ السَّاعَة الْوَاحِدَة وَالنِّصْف مُمْكِنَة؟
lines.en: Wednesday is great. Is half past one possible?

lines.ar: دَقِيقَة وَاحِدَة، مِنْ فَضْلِكَ… آسِفَة، فِي السَّاعَة الْوَاحِدَة وَالنِّصْف عِنْدَهُ اِجْتِمَاع.
lines.en: One minute, please… Sorry, at half past one he has a meeting.

lines.ar: هَلِ السَّاعَة الثَّالِثَة إِلَّا رُبْعًا مُمْكِنَة لَكَ؟
lines.en: Is quarter to three possible for you?

lines.ar: نَعَم، هٰذَا وَقْت مُمْتَاز. الدَّرْس حَتَّى السَّاعَة الْوَاحِدَة فَقَطْ.
lines.en: Yes, that is an excellent time. The lesson only goes on until one o'clock.

lines.ar: إِذَنْ، مَوْعِدُكَ يَوْمَ الْأَرْبِعَاء فِي السَّاعَة الثَّالِثَة إِلَّا رُبْعًا.
lines.en: So, your appointment is on Wednesday at quarter to three.

lines.ar: الْأَرْبِعَاء، الثَّالِثَة إِلَّا رُبْعًا. هَلْ تُرِيدِينَ رَقْمَ هَاتِفِي؟
lines.en: Wednesday, quarter to three. Would you like my phone number?

lines.ar: لَا، شُكْرًا، رَقْمُكَ عِنْدِي. إِلَى اللِّقَاء يَوْمَ الْأَرْبِعَاء!
lines.en: No, thank you, I already have your number. See you on Wednesday!

lines.ar: شُكْرًا جَزِيلًا يَا أُسْتَاذَة! مَعَ السَّلَامَة.
lines.en: Thank you very much, madam! Goodbye.

mistakes.why: The object of a verb takes -an (mawʿidan), and 'on' a day is yawma, with -a.
sāʿa is feminine, so 'possible' takes ة: mumkina.

quiz.prompt: Who does Daniel want to see?
When is Daniel's appointment?
What does this mean?
options: I have a meeting with the director.
I would like an appointment with the director.

quiz.prompt: Why is half past one not possible?

title: Dinner for two
intro: You have dinner with a friend in a restaurant in Cairo. Useful phrases: طَاوِلَة لِاثْنَيْنِ (a table for two), الْقَائِمَة (the menu) and الْحِسَاب (the bill).

dialogue.title: A table for two
dialogue.culture: Many Egyptian restaurants add a service charge to the bill, and people often leave a small tip for the waiter as well. Speaking to two people, the waiter uses the dual: تَفَضَّلَا and شُكْرًا لَكُمَا.

lines.ar: مَسَاءُ الْخَيْر! أَهْلًا بِكَ فِي مَطْعَمِنَا. كَمْ شَخْصًا؟
lines.en: Good evening! Welcome to our restaurant. How many people?

lines.ar: مَسَاءُ النُّور! نَحْنُ شَخْصَانِ: أَنَا وَصَدِيقِي. طَاوِلَة لِاثْنَيْنِ، مِنْ فَضْلِكَ.
lines.en: Good evening! There are two of us: me and my friend. A table for two, please.

lines.ar: تَفَضَّلَا، هٰذِهِ طَاوِلَة جَمِيلَة بِجَانِبِ الشُّبَّاك. وَهٰذِهِ الْقَائِمَة.
lines.en: Please sit down, here is a nice table by the window. And here is the menu.
segs: please, here you are (to two people)

lines.ar: شُكْرًا. مَا هٰذَا الطَّبَق؟ هَلْ فِيهِ لَحْم؟
lines.en: Thank you. What is this dish? Is there meat in it?

lines.ar: هٰذِهِ مُلُوخِيَّة بِالدَّجَاج. وَعِنْدَنَا أَيْضًا مَحْشِي بِدُونِ لَحْم.
lines.en: This is molokhia with chicken. We also have stuffed vegetables without meat.

lines.ar: إِذَنْ نُرِيدُ طَبَقَيْنِ مِنَ الْمَحْشِي، وَسَلَطَةً خَضْرَاء، مِنْ فَضْلِكَ.
lines.en: Then we'd like two plates of stuffed vegetables and a green salad, please.

lines.ar: وَمَاذَا تَشْرَبَانِ؟ عِنْدَنَا عَصِير وَمَاء وَمَشْرُوبَات بَارِدَة.
lines.en: And what will you two drink? We have juice, water and cold drinks.

lines.ar: زُجَاجَتَيْنِ مِنَ الْمَاء، لَوْ سَمَحْتَ. وَهَلِ الطَّعَام حَارّ؟
lines.en: Two bottles of water, please. And is the food spicy?

lines.ar: لَا، لَيْسَ حَارًّا. وَالصَّلْصَة الْحَارَّة عَلَى الطَّاوِلَة.
lines.en: No, it isn't spicy. And the hot sauce is on the table.

lines.ar: الْمَحْشِي لَذِيذ جِدًّا! الْحِسَاب، مِنْ فَضْلِكَ.
lines.en: The stuffed vegetables are delicious! The bill, please.

lines.ar: الْحِسَاب مِئَة وَعِشْرُونَ جُنَيْهًا. شُكْرًا لَكُمَا!
lines.en: The bill is a hundred and twenty pounds. Thank you both!

lines.ar: تَفَضَّلْ. شُكْرًا لَكَ، وَالطَّبَّاخُونَ هُنَا مُمْتَازُونَ!
lines.en: Here you are. Thank you, and the cooks here are excellent!

mistakes.why: After a verb the dual ends in -ayni, not -āni.
The noun follows the last number: after twenty it is singular with -an.

quiz.prompt: How many people are at Daniel's table?
What does this mean?
How much is the bill?

title: At the bakery
intro: You buy bread and pastries early in the morning at a bakery in Cairo. Useful phrases: أُرِيدُ (I'd like), بِكَمْ؟ (how much?) and الْبَاقِي (the change).

dialogue.title: Five loaves and two croissants
dialogue.culture: Bread is so important in Egypt that in everyday speech it is called 'ʿaysh', which means 'life'. Bakeries sell it hot in the morning, and round biscuits called kaʿk are a favourite treat, especially at Eid.

lines.ar: صَبَاحُ الْخَيْر يَا آنِسَة! الْخُبْز طَازَج وَسَاخِن الْآن.
lines.en: Good morning, miss! The bread is fresh and hot right now.

lines.ar: صَبَاحُ النُّور! أُرِيدُ خَمْسَةَ أَرْغِفَة مِنَ الْخُبْز الْبَلَدِيّ، مِنْ فَضْلِكَ.
lines.en: Good morning! I'd like five loaves of country bread, please.

lines.ar: حَاضِر! هَلْ تُرِيدِينَ شَيْئًا آخَر؟ عِنْدَنَا كَعْك وَكَرْوَاسُون.
lines.en: Certainly! Would you like anything else? We have kaʿk biscuits and croissants.

lines.ar: بِكَمِ الْكَرْوَاسُون؟ وَبِكَمِ الْكَعْكَة؟
lines.en: How much is a croissant? And how much is one kaʿk?

lines.ar: الْكَرْوَاسُون بِخَمْسَةَ عَشَرَ جُنَيْهًا، وَالْكَعْكَة بِعَشَرَة جُنَيْهَات.
lines.en: A croissant is fifteen pounds, and a kaʿk is ten pounds.

lines.ar: إِذَنْ أُرِيدُ قِطْعَتَيْنِ مِنَ الْكَرْوَاسُون، وَثَلَاثَ كَعْكَات.
lines.en: Then I'd like two croissants and three kaʿk biscuits.

lines.ar: تَفَضَّلِي: خَمْسَةُ أَرْغِفَة، وَقِطْعَتَانِ مِنَ الْكَرْوَاسُون، وَثَلَاثُ كَعْكَات.
lines.en: Here you are: five loaves, two croissants and three kaʿk biscuits.

lines.ar: شُكْرًا! كَمِ الْحِسَاب، مِنْ فَضْلِكَ؟
lines.en: Thank you! How much is the bill, please?

lines.ar: الْخُبْز بِعَشَرَة، وَالْكَرْوَاسُون بِثَلَاثِينَ، وَالْكَعْك بِثَلَاثِينَ. الْمَجْمُوع سَبْعُونَ جُنَيْهًا.
lines.en: The bread is ten, the croissants thirty and the kaʿk thirty. That's seventy pounds altogether.

lines.ar: تَفَضَّلْ، هٰذِهِ مِئَةُ جُنَيْه.
lines.en: Here you are, this is a hundred pounds.

lines.ar: وَهٰذَا الْبَاقِي: ثَلَاثُونَ جُنَيْهًا. بِالْهَنَاء وَالشِّفَاء!
lines.en: And here is your change: thirty pounds. Enjoy!

lines.ar: شُكْرًا جَزِيلًا! رَائِحَةُ الْخُبْز جَمِيلَة جِدًّا.
lines.en: Thank you very much! The bread smells wonderful.

mistakes.why: After the numbers three to ten the noun is plural.
After 11 to 99 the noun is singular with the ending -an.

quiz.prompt: How many loaves of bread does Layla buy?
How much is one croissant?
What does this mean?

title: Asking the way
intro: You are in downtown Cairo and want to walk to the nearest metro station. Useful phrases: لَوْ سَمَحْتَ (excuse me), أَيْنَ…؟ (where is…?), يَمِينًا (to the right), يَسَارًا (to the left) and الشَّارِع الثَّانِي (the second street).

dialogue.title: Which way to the metro?
dialogue.culture: The Cairo metro is marked by a big red sign with the letter م (mīm, for مِتْرُو). Many station names are famous people or places: Sadat station lies under Tahrir Square.

lines.ar: لَوْ سَمَحْتَ! أَيْنَ مَحَطَّةُ الْمِتْرُو، مِنْ فَضْلِكَ؟
lines.en: Excuse me! Where is the metro station, please?

lines.ar: مَحَطَّةُ السَّادَات؟ هِيَ قَرِيبَة، فِي مَيْدَانِ التَّحْرِير.
lines.en: Sadat station? It is close, in Tahrir Square.
segs: Sadat (a metro station, named after an Egyptian president)

lines.ar: هَلْ هِيَ بَعِيدَة مَشْيًا؟ أَنَا لَا أَعْرِفُ هٰذِهِ الْمِنْطَقَة.
lines.en: Is it far on foot? I don't know this area.

lines.ar: لَا، عَشْرُ دَقَائِق فَقَطْ. اِذْهَبِي إِلَى الْأَمَام حَتَّى الْإِشَارَة.
lines.en: No, only ten minutes. Go straight ahead as far as the traffic lights.

lines.ar: حَتَّى الْإِشَارَة، ثُمَّ يَمِينًا أَمْ يَسَارًا؟
lines.en: As far as the traffic lights, and then right or left?

lines.ar: ثُمَّ خُذِي الشَّارِعَ الثَّانِي عَلَى الْيَسَار.
lines.en: Then take the second street on the left.

lines.ar: الشَّارِع الثَّانِي عَلَى الْيَسَار. وَبَعْدَ ذٰلِكَ؟
lines.en: The second street on the left. And after that?

lines.ar: بَعْدَ ذٰلِكَ تَرَيْنَ الْمَيْدَان. الْمَحَطَّة أَمَامَ الْمَتْحَف الْمِصْرِيّ تَقْرِيبًا.
lines.en: After that you will see the square. The station is more or less in front of the Egyptian Museum.

lines.ar: هَلْ هُنَاكَ عَلَامَة لِلْمِتْرُو؟
lines.en: Is there a sign for the metro?

lines.ar: نَعَم، هُنَاكَ عَلَامَة حَمْرَاء كَبِيرَة عَلَيْهَا حَرْف «م».
lines.en: Yes, there is a big red sign with the letter M on it.

lines.ar: شُكْرًا جَزِيلًا! أَنْتَ لَطِيف جِدًّا.
lines.en: Thank you very much! You are very kind.

lines.ar: عَفْوًا! مَعَ السَّلَامَة، وَانْتَبِهِي مِنَ السَّيَّارَات!
lines.en: You're welcome! Goodbye, and watch out for the cars!

mistakes.why: Speaking to a woman, the command ends in -ī: idhhabī, khudhī.
An ordinal comes after its noun, like any adjective.

quiz.prompt: Where is the metro station?
Which way does Layla go after the traffic lights?
options: the first street on the right
the third street on the left
the second street on the left
the second street on the right

quiz.prompt: What does this mean?

title: In a clothes shop
intro: You are buying a dress in a clothes shop in Cairo. Useful phrases: مَقَاس (size), ضَيِّق (tight), وَاسِع (loose), أُرِيدُ (I want) and بِكَمْ؟ (how much is it?).

dialogue.title: A dress for a party
dialogue.culture: Many clothes shops in Egypt stay open until late at night, and evening is the busiest time for shopping, especially in summer when the days are hot.

lines.ar: مَسَاءُ الْخَيْر! تَفَضَّلِي. هَلْ تَبْحَثِينَ عَنْ شَيْء خَاصّ؟
lines.en: Good evening! Come in. Are you looking for something special?

lines.ar: مَسَاءُ النُّور. أُرِيدُ فُسْتَانًا لِحَفْلَةِ عِيدِ مِيلَاد.
lines.en: Good evening. I would like a dress for a birthday party.

lines.ar: عِنْدَنَا فَسَاتِين جَدِيدَة كَثِيرَة. هٰذِهِ الْفَسَاتِين الْخَضْرَاء جَمِيلَة جِدًّا.
lines.en: We have lots of new dresses. These green dresses are very pretty.

lines.ar: نَعَم، هِيَ جَمِيلَة. هَلْ عِنْدَكَ هٰذَا الْفُسْتَان بِمَقَاس صَغِير؟
lines.en: Yes, they are pretty. Do you have this dress in a small size?

lines.ar: طَبْعًا، تَفَضَّلِي. غُرْفَةُ الْقِيَاس هُنَاكَ، عَلَى الْيَمِين.
lines.en: Of course, here you are. The fitting room is over there, on the right.

lines.ar: لِلْأَسَف، الْفُسْتَان ضَيِّق قَلِيلًا. هَلْ هُنَاكَ مَقَاس أَكْبَر؟
lines.en: Unfortunately, the dress is a little tight. Is there a bigger size?

lines.ar: نَعَم، هٰذَا الْمَقَاس الْمُتَوَسِّط. هُوَ مُنَاسِب لَكِ، إِنْ شَاءَ اللّٰه.
lines.en: Yes, this is the medium size. It should be right for you, God willing.

lines.ar: مُمْتَاز! هٰذَا الْمَقَاس جَيِّد: لَا ضَيِّق وَلَا وَاسِع. بِكَمْ هُوَ؟
lines.en: Excellent! This size is good: neither tight nor loose. How much is it?

lines.ar: بِسَبْعِمِئَة جُنَيْه. وَعِنْدَنَا أَيْضًا أَحْذِيَة مُنَاسِبَة لِلْفُسْتَان.
lines.en: Seven hundred pounds. And we also have shoes that go with the dress.

lines.ar: لَا، شُكْرًا. عِنْدِي أَحْذِيَة كَثِيرَة فِي الْبَيْت!
lines.en: No, thank you. I have lots of shoes at home!

lines.ar: كَمَا تُحِبِّينَ. تَفَضَّلِي، الْفُسْتَان فِي الْحَقِيبَة. مَبْرُوك!
lines.en: As you like. Here you are, the dress is in the bag. Enjoy it!

lines.ar: شُكْرًا جَزِيلًا! مَعَ السَّلَامَة.
lines.en: Thank you very much! Goodbye.

mistakes.why: Plurals of things take a feminine singular adjective.
fustān (dress) is masculine, even though women wear it.

quiz.prompt: What does Layla want to buy?
What is wrong with the first dress?
What does this mean?

title: Renting a flat
intro: You look round a furnished flat with the owner and ask about the rooms, the furniture and the rent. Useful phrases: هَلِ الشَّقَّة مَفْرُوشَة؟ (is the flat furnished?), هَلْ فِيهِ …؟ (is there … in it?) and كَمِ الْإِيجَار؟ (how much is the rent?).

dialogue.title: A flat with a view
dialogue.culture: Students in Egypt often rent a شَقَّة مَفْرُوشَة (furnished flat). The owner usually asks for the first month's rent and a deposit (تَأْمِين) before handing over the key.

lines.ar: أَهْلًا وَسَهْلًا! أَنْتَ دَانْيَال؟ تَفَضَّلْ، هٰذِهِ هِيَ الشَّقَّة.
lines.en: Welcome! Are you Daniel? Please come in, this is the flat.

lines.ar: شُكْرًا يَا أُسْتَاذ مَحْمُود. هَلِ الشَّقَّة مَفْرُوشَة؟
lines.en: Thank you, Mr Mahmoud. Is the flat furnished?

lines.ar: نَعَم، فِيهَا سَرِير وَمَكْتَب وَخِزَانَة، وَفِي غُرْفَةِ الْجُلُوس كَنَبَة.
lines.en: Yes, there is a bed, a desk and a wardrobe, and there is a sofa in the living room.

lines.ar: وَالْمَطْبَخ؟ هَلْ فِيهِ ثَلَّاجَة؟
lines.en: And the kitchen? Is there a fridge in it?

lines.ar: الْمَطْبَخ صَغِير، وَلَيْسَ فِيهِ ثَلَّاجَة، لٰكِنْ فِيهِ فُرْن جَدِيد.
lines.en: The kitchen is small, and there is no fridge, but there is a new oven.

lines.ar: لَا مُشْكِلَة. وَالْحَمَّام؟ هَلْ فِيهِ مَاء سَاخِن؟
lines.en: No problem. And the bathroom? Is there hot water?

lines.ar: طَبْعًا! وَهٰذِهِ الشُّرْفَة. اُنْظُرْ، مِنْ هُنَا تَرَى النِّيل.
lines.en: Of course! And this is the balcony. Look, from here you can see the Nile.

lines.ar: جَمِيل جِدًّا! كَمِ الْإِيجَار فِي الشَّهْر، مِنْ فَضْلِكَ؟
lines.en: Very beautiful! How much is the rent per month, please?

lines.ar: سَبْعَةُ آلَافِ جُنَيْه فِي الشَّهْر، وَالتَّأْمِين شَهْر وَاحِد.
lines.en: Seven thousand pounds a month, and the deposit is one month's rent.

lines.ar: هٰذَا مُنَاسِب. هَلِ الْكَهْرَبَاء وَالْمَاء مَعَ الْإِيجَار؟
lines.en: That's fine. Are electricity and water included in the rent?

lines.ar: لَا، الْكَهْرَبَاء عَلَيْكَ، وَالْمَاء عَلَيَّ.
lines.en: No, you pay for the electricity, and I pay for the water.
segs: on you: your cost (to a man)

lines.ar: اِتَّفَقْنَا! مَتَى أَسْتَطِيعُ أَنْ أَسْكُنَ هُنَا؟
lines.en: It's a deal! When can I move in?

lines.ar: غَدًا، إِنْ شَاءَ اللّٰه. تَفَضَّلْ، هٰذَا مِفْتَاحُ الشَّقَّة. مَبْرُوك!
lines.en: Tomorrow, God willing. Here you are, this is the key to the flat. Congratulations!

lines.ar: اللّٰه يُبَارِكُ فِيكَ! شُكْرًا جَزِيلًا يَا أُسْتَاذ مَحْمُود.
lines.en: God bless you! Thank you very much, Mr Mahmoud.

mistakes.why: To ask 'is there a …?', the thing has no الـ.
You ask about 'the rent', so use الـ: كَمِ الْإِيجَار؟ The m of كَمْ takes an i to link to it.

quiz.prompt: How do you ask 'Is the flat furnished?'
What is missing in the kitchen?
What does this mean?
options: The electricity is on the balcony.

title: Visiting a family
intro: You are a guest in an Egyptian family home. Greet everyone, accept tea politely and compliment the home. Useful phrases: بَيْتُكُمْ جَمِيل (your home is beautiful), تَفَضَّلْ (please, come in) and يَكْفِي (that's enough).

dialogue.title: Tea with Sami's parents
dialogue.culture: A guest brings a small gift, often sweets (حَلَوِيَّات). The hosts will offer food again and again: it is polite to accept a little, and to say يَكْفِي، شُكْرًا (that's enough, thank you) when you are really full.

lines.ar: أَهْلًا وَسَهْلًا يَا دَانْيَال! تَفَضَّلْ، الْبَيْت بَيْتُكَ.
lines.en: Welcome, Daniel! Please come in and make yourself at home.

lines.ar: شُكْرًا يَا أُسْتَاذ أَحْمَد. هٰذِهِ حَلَوِيَّات لَكُمْ.
lines.en: Thank you, Mr Ahmad. These sweets are for you.

lines.ar: شُكْرًا، لِمَاذَا أَتْعَبْتَ نَفْسَكَ؟ تَفَضَّلْ، اِجْلِسْ هُنَا.
lines.en: Thank you, you shouldn't have! Please, sit here.
segs: you tired, you troubled (to a man)

lines.ar: أَهْلًا يَا دَانْيَال! مَاذَا تَشْرَبُ؟ عِنْدَنَا شَاي وَقَهْوَة وَعَصِير.
lines.en: Hello, Daniel! What would you like to drink? We have tea, coffee and juice.

lines.ar: شَاي، مِنْ فَضْلِكِ، بِدُونِ سُكَّر. بَيْتُكُمْ جَمِيل جِدًّا!
lines.en: Tea, please, without sugar. Your home is very beautiful!

lines.ar: شُكْرًا! هٰذِهِ غُرْفَةُ الْجُلُوس، وَتِلْكَ غُرْفَةُ الطَّعَام.
lines.en: Thank you! This is the living room, and that is the dining room.

lines.ar: كَيْفَ شَقَّتُكَ الْجَدِيدَة يَا دَانْيَال؟ هَلْ هِيَ مُرِيحَة؟
lines.en: How is your new flat, Daniel? Is it comfortable?

lines.ar: هِيَ صَغِيرَة، لٰكِنَّهَا مُرِيحَة، وَعِنْدِي شُرْفَة عَلَى النِّيل.
lines.en: It's small, but it's comfortable, and I have a balcony overlooking the Nile.

lines.ar: تَفَضَّلِ الشَّاي، وَخُذْ قِطْعَة كَعْك أُخْرَى!
lines.en: Here's your tea, and have another piece of cake!

lines.ar: شُكْرًا جَزِيلًا، الْكَعْك لَذِيذ، لٰكِنْ يَكْفِي، أَنَا شَبْعَان!
lines.en: Thank you so much, the cake is delicious, but that's enough, I'm full!

lines.ar: لَا، لَا! أَنْتَ نَحِيف جِدًّا. كُلْ، كُلْ!
lines.en: No, no! You're far too thin. Eat, eat!

lines.ar: حَاضِر يَا دُكْتُورَة! قِطْعَة صَغِيرَة فَقَطْ، مِنْ فَضْلِكِ.
lines.en: All right, doctor! Just a small piece, please.

lines.ar: يَا دَانْيَال، بَيْتُنَا مَفْتُوح لَكَ دَائِمًا. أَنْتَ مِنَ الْعَائِلَة الْآن.
lines.en: Daniel, our home is always open to you. You're one of the family now.

lines.ar: شُكْرًا لَكُمْ، أَنْتُمْ عَائِلَة كَرِيمَة جِدًّا.
lines.en: Thank you all, you are a very generous family.

mistakes.why: Speaking to the whole family, use ـُكُمْ (your, to several people).
-ki for a woman, -ka for a man.

quiz.prompt: How do you compliment the family on their home?
What does Daniel bring as a gift?
What does this mean?

title: Lost luggage
intro: You come back to Cairo from Alexandria by train and realise that you left your bag on the train. At the lost property office in Ramses Station, explain what happened. Useful phrases: نَسِيتُ (I forgot), لَمْ أَجِدْهَا (I didn't find it) and كَانَ فِيهَا (there was in it).

dialogue.title: A blue bag in carriage four
dialogue.culture: Ramses Station is Cairo's main railway station, named after the pharaoh Ramses II. Trains to Alexandria leave from here many times a day.

lines.ar: مَسَاءُ الْخَيْر، مَكْتَبُ الْمَفْقُودَات. كَيْفَ أُسَاعِدُكَ؟
lines.en: Good evening, lost property office. How can I help you?

lines.ar: مَسَاءُ النُّور. نَسِيتُ حَقِيبَتِي فِي قِطَارِ الْإِسْكَنْدَرِيَّة، وَلَمْ أَجِدْهَا.
lines.en: Good evening. I left my bag on the train from Alexandria, and I couldn't find it.

lines.ar: مَتَى وَصَلَ الْقِطَار؟ وَفِي أَيِّ عَرَبَة جَلَسْتَ؟
lines.en: When did the train arrive? And which carriage did you sit in?

lines.ar: وَصَلَ فِي السَّاعَة التَّاسِعَة مَسَاءً. جَلَسْتُ فِي الْعَرَبَة رَقْم أَرْبَعَة.
lines.en: It arrived at nine in the evening. I sat in carriage number four.

lines.ar: وَلِمَاذَا لَمْ تَأْخُذِ الْحَقِيبَة مَعَكَ؟ هَلْ نِمْتَ فِي الْقِطَار؟
lines.en: And why didn't you take the bag with you? Did you fall asleep on the train?

lines.ar: نَعَم، نِمْتُ قَلِيلًا، وَبَعْدَ أَنْ وَصَلْنَا خَرَجْتُ بِسُرْعَة مَعَ صَدِيقِي.
lines.en: Yes, I slept a little, and after we arrived I got off in a hurry with my friend.
segs: I went out, I got off

lines.ar: مَا لَوْنُ الْحَقِيبَة؟ وَمَاذَا كَانَ فِيهَا؟
lines.en: What colour is the bag? And what was in it?

lines.ar: هِيَ حَقِيبَة زَرْقَاء صَغِيرَة. كَانَ فِيهَا كِتَاب وَكَامِيرَا وَمِفْتَاحُ شَقَّتِي.
lines.en: It's a small blue bag. There was a book in it, a camera and the key to my flat.

lines.ar: لَحْظَة، مِنْ فَضْلِكَ… الْعُمَّال لَمْ يَذْهَبُوا بَعْدُ. سَأَسْأَلُهُمْ.
lines.en: One moment, please… The workers haven't gone home yet. I'll ask them.

lines.ar: أَنْتَ مَحْظُوظ! وَجَدُوا حَقِيبَة زَرْقَاء فِي الْعَرَبَة رَقْم أَرْبَعَة. هَلْ هٰذِهِ حَقِيبَتُكَ؟
lines.en: You're lucky! They found a blue bag in carriage number four. Is this your bag?

lines.ar: نَعَم، هٰذِهِ هِيَ! الْحَمْدُ لِلّٰه! شُكْرًا جَزِيلًا.
lines.en: Yes, that's the one! Thank God! Thank you very much.

lines.ar: عَفْوًا. فِي الْمَرَّة الْقَادِمَة لَا تَنَمْ فِي الْقِطَار!
lines.en: You're welcome. Next time, don't fall asleep on the train!

mistakes.why: After لَمْ the verb loses its final -u: lam ajid-hā, not lam ajidu-hā.
حَقِيبَة is feminine, so the colour is feminine too: zarqāʾ.

quiz.prompt: Where did Daniel leave his bag?
What was in the bag?
options: a book, a camera and his flat key

quiz.prompt: What does this mean?

title: How was your holiday?
intro: After the mid-term break your classmate Huda asks about your holiday. Tell her where you went, how you travelled and what it was like. Useful phrases: سَافَرْتُ (I travelled), كَانَتِ الرِّحْلَةُ … (the trip was …) and لَمْ نَذْهَبْ (we didn't go).

dialogue.title: Luxor and Aswan
dialogue.culture: Luxor (الْأُقْصُر) is full of ancient Egyptian temples, and at sunrise dozens of hot-air balloons float over the Nile and the Valley of the Kings. Many visitors take the overnight sleeper train from Cairo.

lines.ar: أَهْلًا يَا دَانْيَال! كَيْفَ كَانَتْ عُطْلَتُكَ؟ أَيْنَ ذَهَبْتَ؟
lines.en: Hi, Daniel! How was your holiday? Where did you go?

lines.ar: كَانَتْ رَائِعَةً! سَافَرْتُ مَعَ صَدِيقِي إِلَى الْأُقْصُر وَأَسْوَان.
lines.en: It was wonderful! I travelled to Luxor and Aswan with my friend.

lines.ar: مَا شَاءَ اللّٰه! كَيْفَ سَافَرْتُمَا؟ لَمْ تَذْهَبْ بِالطَّائِرَة، صَحِيح؟
lines.en: How lovely! How did you two travel? You didn't go by plane, did you?
segs: you go (to a man; form after 'lam')

lines.ar: لَا، لَمْ نَذْهَبْ بِالطَّائِرَة. رَكِبْنَا قِطَارَ اللَّيْل، وَكَانَتِ الرِّحْلَةُ طَوِيلَةً.
lines.en: No, we didn't go by plane. We took the night train, and the journey was long.

lines.ar: وَمَاذَا فَعَلْتُمَا فِي الْأُقْصُر؟
lines.en: And what did you two do in Luxor?

lines.ar: زُرْنَا الْمَعَابِد الْقَدِيمَة، وَفِي الصَّبَاح الْبَاكِر رَكِبْنَا مُنْطَادًا فَوْقَ النِّيل.
lines.en: We visited the ancient temples, and early in the morning we went up in a balloon over the Nile.

lines.ar: يَا سَلَام! وَهَلْ كَانَ الْجَوُّ حَارًّا هُنَاكَ؟
lines.en: Wow! And was the weather hot there?

lines.ar: كَانَ حَارًّا فِي النَّهَار، لٰكِنْ لَطِيفًا فِي الْمَسَاء. وَأَنْتِ؟ لَمْ تَذْهَبِي إِلَى أَيِّ مَكَان؟
lines.en: It was hot in the daytime but pleasant in the evening. And you? Didn't you go anywhere?
segs: you go (to a woman; form after 'lam')

lines.ar: لَا، لَمْ أُسَافِرْ. زَارَنَا أَقَارِبِي مِنَ الْإِسْكَنْدَرِيَّة، وَهُمْ بَقُوا عِنْدَنَا أُسْبُوعًا كَامِلًا.
lines.en: No, I didn't travel. My relatives from Alexandria visited us, and they stayed with us for a whole week.

lines.ar: وَهَلْ خَرَجْتُمْ مَعًا يَا هُدَى؟
lines.en: And did you all go out together, Huda?

lines.ar: نَعَم، ذَهَبْنَا إِلَى الْأَهْرَام. لٰكِنْ أَخِي لَمْ يَذْهَبْ مَعَنَا، لِأَنَّهُ كَانَ مَرِيضًا.
lines.en: Yes, we went to the pyramids. But my brother didn't come with us, because he was ill.

lines.ar: سَلَامَتُهُ! أَرْجُو أَنْ يَكُونَ بِخَيْر الْآنَ.
lines.en: I'm sorry he was ill! I hope he is well now.

mistakes.why: After كَانَ or كَانَتْ the description takes the -an ending: ṭawīlatan.
لَمْ takes the present form with a sukūn at the end, not the past.

quiz.prompt: Where did Daniel travel in the holiday?
How did Daniel and his friend travel?
What does this mean?
options: Didn't you go anywhere? (to a woman)
You didn't go to the place.

title: At the doctor's
intro: Layla has a sore throat and a temperature, so she sees a doctor in Cairo. Useful phrases: يُؤْلِمُنِي حَلْقِي (my throat hurts), عِنْدِي حَرَارَة (I have a temperature) and مُنْذُ يَوْمَيْنِ (for two days).

dialogue.title: A sore throat
dialogue.culture: At a private clinic in Egypt you usually pay the consultation fee at reception before you see the doctor. Keep the prescription: the pharmacist will need it.

lines.ar: تَفَضَّلِي، اِجْلِسِي هُنَا. مِمَّ تَشْكِينَ؟
lines.en: Please come in and sit here. What seems to be the problem?

lines.ar: يُؤْلِمُنِي حَلْقِي كَثِيرًا، وَعِنْدِي حَرَارَة مُنْذُ يَوْمَيْنِ.
lines.en: My throat hurts a lot, and I have had a temperature for two days.

lines.ar: هَلْ عِنْدَكِ سُعَال أَوْ صُدَاع أَيْضًا؟
lines.en: Do you also have a cough or a headache?

lines.ar: عِنْدِي صُدَاع فِي الْمَسَاء، لٰكِنْ لَيْسَ عِنْدِي سُعَال.
lines.en: I have a headache in the evening, but I don't have a cough.

lines.ar: طَيِّب. اِفْتَحِي فَمَكِ، مِنْ فَضْلِكِ… حَلْقُكِ أَحْمَر جِدًّا.
lines.en: OK. Open your mouth, please… Your throat is very red.

lines.ar: هَلْ هٰذَا خَطِير يَا دُكْتُور؟
lines.en: Is it serious, doctor?

lines.ar: لَا، لَا تَقْلَقِي. حَلْقُكِ مُلْتَهِب فَقَطْ، وَهٰذَا لَيْسَ خَطِيرًا.
lines.en: No, don't worry. Your throat is just inflamed, and that isn't serious.

lines.ar: تَنَفَّسِي بِعُمْق… الصَّدْر سَلِيم، الْحَمْدُ لِلّٰه.
lines.en: Breathe deeply… Your chest is fine, thank God.

lines.ar: هَلْ يَجِبُ أَنْ آخُذَ دَوَاءً؟
lines.en: Do I have to take any medicine?

lines.ar: نَعَم، هٰذِهِ وَصْفَة: حَبَّة مَرَّتَيْنِ فِي الْيَوْم، خَمْسَةَ أَيَّام.
lines.en: Yes, here is a prescription: one tablet twice a day for five days.

lines.ar: وَلَا تَشْرَبِي مَشْرُوبَات بَارِدَة، وَارْتَاحِي فِي الْبَيْت.
lines.en: And don't drink cold drinks, and rest at home.

lines.ar: شُكْرًا جَزِيلًا يَا دُكْتُور، مَعَ السَّلَامَة.
lines.en: Thank you very much, doctor. Goodbye.

lines.ar: مَعَ السَّلَامَة، وَسَلَامَتُكِ!
lines.en: Goodbye, and get well soon!
segs: and get well soon (to a woman)

mistakes.why: ḥalq (throat) is masculine, so the verb starts with yu-.
An order to a woman ends in -ī: iftaḥī.

quiz.prompt: How long has Layla had a temperature?
What does the doctor say Layla has?
What does this mean?

title: At the pharmacy
intro: Sami's little sister Nour has a cough, so Sami goes to the pharmacy near his home. Useful phrases: أُرِيدُ أَنْ أَشْتَرِيَ (I want to buy), كَمْ مَرَّةً (how many times) and لِلْأَطْفَال (for children).

dialogue.title: Medicine for Nour
dialogue.culture: Pharmacists in the Arab world give a lot of advice, and some simple medicines can be bought without a prescription. Always tell the pharmacist the age of the patient, especially for a child.

lines.ar: صَبَاحُ الْخَيْر! كَيْفَ أَسْتَطِيعُ أَنْ أُسَاعِدَكَ؟
lines.en: Good morning! How can I help you?

lines.ar: صَبَاحُ النُّور. أُرِيدُ أَنْ أَشْتَرِيَ دَوَاءً لِلسُّعَال لِأُخْتِي الصَّغِيرَة.
lines.en: Good morning. I want to buy some cough medicine for my little sister.

lines.ar: كَمْ عُمْرُهَا؟ وَهَلْ عِنْدَهَا حَرَارَة؟
lines.en: How old is she? And does she have a temperature?

lines.ar: عُمْرُهَا سِتّ سَنَوَات، وَلَيْسَ عِنْدَهَا حَرَارَة، الْحَمْدُ لِلّٰه.
lines.en: She is six years old, and she doesn't have a temperature, thank God.

lines.ar: إِذَنْ هٰذَا الشَّرَاب جَيِّد لِلْأَطْفَال، وَهُوَ بِطَعْمِ الْفَرَاوِلَة.
lines.en: Then this syrup is good for children, and it tastes of strawberry.

lines.ar: مُمْتَاز! نُور تُحِبُّ الْفَرَاوِلَة. كَمْ مَرَّةً فِي الْيَوْم؟
lines.en: Excellent! Nour loves strawberries. How many times a day?

lines.ar: مِلْعَقَة صَغِيرَة ثَلَاثَ مَرَّات فِي الْيَوْم، بَعْدَ الْأَكْل.
lines.en: One small spoonful three times a day, after food.

lines.ar: وَلَا تُعْطِهَا أَكْثَرَ مِنْ ثَلَاثِ مَلَاعِق فِي الْيَوْم.
lines.en: And don't give her more than three spoonfuls a day.

lines.ar: فَهِمْتُ. وَهَلْ تَبِيعُونَ مَنَادِيل وَعَسَلًا أَيْضًا؟
lines.en: I see. And do you sell tissues and honey too?

lines.ar: الْمَنَادِيل هُنَاكَ، لٰكِنْ لَيْسَ عِنْدَنَا عَسَل، آسِف.
lines.en: The tissues are over there, but we don't have any honey, sorry.

lines.ar: لَا مُشْكِلَة. كَمِ الْحِسَاب، مِنْ فَضْلِكَ؟
lines.en: No problem. How much is that, please?

lines.ar: خَمْسَة وَأَرْبَعُونَ جُنَيْهًا. سَلَامَتُهَا!
lines.en: Forty-five pounds. I hope she gets well soon!
segs: (wishing) her safety: 'get well soon' (about a woman)

lines.ar: شُكْرًا، اللّٰهُ يُسَلِّمُكَ. مَعَ السَّلَامَة!
lines.en: Thanks, God keep you safe. Goodbye!

mistakes.why: Join the two verbs with an, and the second verb ends in -a.
milʿaqa (spoon) is feminine, so the number three has no ة.

quiz.prompt: Who is the medicine for?
How old is Nour?
What does this mean?
How much does Sami pay?

title: A birthday invitation
intro: Your neighbour Huda knocks on your door to invite you to her son's birthday party. Useful phrases: جِئْتُ لِأَدْعُوَكَ (I've come to invite you), بِكُلِّ سُرُور (with pleasure) and كُلُّ عَامٍ وَهُوَ بِخَيْر (happy birthday to him).

dialogue.title: A party in the garden
dialogue.culture: Neighbours in Arab cities often know each other well and invite each other to family celebrations. Children's birthday parties are usually in the late afternoon, with a big cake, candles and the birthday song. A small present is welcome, but nobody expects anything expensive.

lines.ar: مَسَاءُ الْخَيْر يَا دَانْيَال! أَنَا جَارَتُكَ هُدَى، مِنَ الطَّابِق الثَّالِث.
lines.en: Good evening, Daniel! I'm your neighbour Huda, from the third floor.
segs: your neighbour (a woman; to a man)

lines.ar: مَسَاءُ النُّور يَا سَيِّدَة هُدَى! تَفَضَّلِي، كَيْفَ أَسْتَطِيعُ أَنْ أُسَاعِدَكِ؟
lines.en: Good evening, Mrs Huda! Please come in. How can I help you?
segs: I help you (to a woman, after an)

lines.ar: شُكْرًا، لَنْ أَدْخُلَ. جِئْتُ لِأَدْعُوَكَ إِلَى حَفْلَةِ عِيدِ مِيلَادِ وَلَدِي آدَم يَوْمَ السَّبْت.
lines.en: Thank you, I won't come in. I've come to invite you to my son Adam's birthday party on Saturday.

lines.ar: شُكْرًا عَلَى الدَّعْوَة! كُلُّ عَامٍ وَهُوَ بِخَيْر. كَمْ عُمْرُهُ الْآنَ؟
lines.en: Thank you for the invitation! Happy birthday to him. How old is he now?
segs: well ('kullu ʿāmin wa-huwa bi-khayr': happy birthday to him)

lines.ar: سَيَكُونُ عُمْرُهُ سِتَّ سَنَوَات. الْحَفْلَة فِي الْحَدِيقَة أَمَامَ الْبِنَايَة، فِي السَّاعَة الْخَامِسَة.
lines.en: He'll be six years old. The party is in the garden in front of the building, at five o'clock.

lines.ar: يَوْمَ السَّبْت فِي السَّاعَة الْخَامِسَة؟ لَا مُشْكِلَة، لَنْ أَكُونَ مَشْغُولًا. سَآتِي بِكُلِّ سُرُور.
lines.en: Saturday at five? No problem, I won't be busy. I'll come with pleasure.

lines.ar: رَائِع! سَيَكُونُ هُنَاكَ أَطْفَال كَثِيرُونَ مِنَ الْبِنَايَة، وَكَعْكَة كَبِيرَة طَبْعًا.
lines.en: Wonderful! There will be lots of children from the building, and a big cake of course.

lines.ar: هَلْ أُحْضِرُ شَيْئًا؟ أُرِيدُ أَنْ أَشْتَرِيَ هَدِيَّة لِآدَم. مَاذَا يُحِبُّ؟
lines.en: Shall I bring something? I'd like to buy a present for Adam. What does he like?

lines.ar: هُوَ يُحِبُّ كُرَةَ الْقَدَم كَثِيرًا، لٰكِنْ لَا تَشْتَرِ شَيْئًا غَالِيًا، مِنْ فَضْلِكَ!
lines.en: He loves football, but please don't buy anything expensive!

lines.ar: إِذَنْ سَأَذْهَبُ إِلَى السُّوق غَدًا لِأَشْتَرِيَ لَهُ كُرَة صَغِيرَة.
lines.en: Then I'll go to the market tomorrow to buy him a small ball.

lines.ar: فِكْرَة جَمِيلَة! سَيَفْرَحُ كَثِيرًا. إِذَنْ نَرَاكَ يَوْمَ السَّبْت.
lines.en: What a lovely idea! He'll be very happy. So we'll see you on Saturday.

lines.ar: إِنْ شَاءَ اللّٰه. شُكْرًا مَرَّةً أُخْرَى، وَمَعَ السَّلَامَة يَا سَيِّدَة هُدَى!
lines.en: God willing. Thank you again, and goodbye, Mrs Huda!

mistakes.why: The future negative is lan + the present ending in -a: lan akūna.
daʿā (to invite) takes the person as an ending, and after li- the verb ends in -a: li-adʿuwaka.

quiz.prompt: Who is the party for?
When is the party?
What does this mean?
What will Daniel buy for Adam?

title: Checking the forecast
intro: Sami wants to take Daniel to the beach at Ain Sokhna on the Red Sea. Before they choose a day, they check the weather forecast. Useful phrases: كَيْفَ سَيَكُونُ الطَّقْس؟ (what will the weather be like?), سَيَكُونُ الْجَوّ مُشْمِسًا (it will be sunny) and لَنْ نَسْبَحَ (we won't swim).

dialogue.title: Friday or Saturday?
dialogue.culture: Ain Sokhna is a beach town on the Red Sea, about two hours by road from Cairo, and a favourite weekend trip for Cairenes. The Red Sea stays warm enough for swimming well into the autumn, but the sun is strong all year: Egyptians rarely go to the beach without a hat and plenty of water.

lines.ar: يَا دَانْيَال، مَا رَأْيُكَ؟ نِهَايَةَ الْأُسْبُوع الْقَادِم سَنَذْهَبُ إِلَى الْبَحْر فِي الْعَيْن السُّخْنَة!
lines.en: Daniel, what do you think? Next weekend we'll go to the sea at Ain Sokhna!
segs: Ain (part of the place name; lit. the spring)
Sokhna (Ain Sokhna: a beach town on the Red Sea)

lines.ar: فِكْرَة رَائِعَة! لٰكِنْ فِي نُوفَمْبِر، هَلْ سَيَكُونُ الْجَوّ دَافِئًا عَلَى الْبَحْر؟
lines.en: A great idea! But in November, will the weather be warm by the sea?

lines.ar: عَادَةً نَعَم، فَالْبَحْر الْأَحْمَر دَافِئ فِي الْخَرِيف. لٰكِنْ سَأَنْظُرُ إِلَى أَخْبَارِ الطَّقْس فِي هَاتِفِي أَوَّلًا.
lines.en: Usually, yes: the Red Sea is warm in autumn. But I'll look at the weather forecast on my phone first.

lines.ar: حَسَنًا. كَيْفَ سَيَكُونُ الطَّقْس يَوْمَ الْجُمُعَة؟
lines.en: All right. What will the weather be like on Friday?

lines.ar: يَوْمَ الْجُمُعَة سَتَكُونُ هُنَاكَ رِيَاح قَوِيَّة، وَرُبَّمَا تُمْطِرُ قَلِيلًا. هٰذَا غَرِيب فِي مِصْر!
lines.en: On Friday there will be strong winds, and it might rain a little. That's strange in Egypt!

lines.ar: رِيَاح وَمَطَر؟ إِذَنْ لَنْ نَسْبَحَ يَوْمَ الْجُمُعَة. وَيَوْمَ السَّبْت؟
lines.en: Wind and rain? Then we won't swim on Friday. And what about Saturday?

lines.ar: يَوْمَ السَّبْت سَيَكُونُ الْجَوّ مُشْمِسًا وَدَافِئًا، وَدَرَجَةُ الْحَرَارَة سِتٌّ وَعِشْرُونَ.
lines.en: On Saturday it will be sunny and warm, and the temperature will be twenty-six degrees.

lines.ar: مُمْتَاز! إِذَنْ سَنَذْهَبُ يَوْمَ السَّبْت. مَتَى سَنَخْرُجُ مِنَ الْقَاهِرَة؟
lines.en: Excellent! So we'll go on Saturday. When will we leave Cairo?
segs: we will go out, we will leave

lines.ar: سَنَخْرُجُ فِي السَّاعَة السَّادِسَة صَبَاحًا لِنَصِلَ قَبْلَ الظُّهْر، فَالطَّرِيق طَوِيل.
lines.en: We'll leave at six in the morning so that we arrive before noon, because the road is long.
segs: we will go out, we will leave

lines.ar: وَمَاذَا نَأْخُذُ مَعَنَا؟ أَنَا لَا أَعْرِفُ الْبَحْر الْأَحْمَر.
lines.en: And what should we take with us? I don't know the Red Sea at all.

lines.ar: خُذْ قُبَّعَة وَمَاءً كَثِيرًا، لِأَنَّ الشَّمْس قَوِيَّة هُنَاكَ. وَخُذْ مِعْطَفًا خَفِيفًا لِلْمَسَاء.
lines.en: Take a hat and lots of water, because the sun is strong there. And take a light jacket for the evening.

lines.ar: اِتَّفَقْنَا! سَأَشْتَرِي قُبَّعَة جَدِيدَة غَدًا. لَنْ أَنْسَى الْمَاء هٰذِهِ الْمَرَّة!
lines.en: Agreed! I'll buy a new hat tomorrow. I won't forget the water this time!

mistakes.why: Name the weather, al-jaww, instead of an empty 'it'; for the future use sa-yakūnu with the -an ending.
The future negative is lan + the present ending in -a, never lā + sa-.

quiz.prompt: Why won't they go on Friday?
options: There will be strong winds and maybe rain.

quiz.prompt: What will the temperature be on Saturday?
What does this mean?
options: so that we arrive before noon

quiz.prompt: What does Sami tell Daniel to take?
options: a hat, lots of water and a light jacket

title: Checking in at the airport
intro: At the end of the trip Daniel checks in at Amman airport for his flight back to Cairo, but his suitcase is full of presents. Useful phrases: جَوَازُ السَّفَر (passport), هَلْ مِنَ الْمُمْكِن أَنْ…؟ (is it possible to…?) and بِطَاقَةُ الصُّعُود (boarding pass).

dialogue.title: A heavy suitcase
dialogue.culture: Queen Alia International Airport is about thirty kilometres south of Amman. Many airlines in the region allow 23 kilos for a suitcase and around seven kilos of hand luggage, and extra weight can be expensive, so weigh your bag before you leave the hotel.

lines.ar: مَسَاءُ الْخَيْر! إِلَى أَيْنَ تُسَافِرُ الْيَوْمَ؟ جَوَازُ السَّفَر وَالتَّذْكِرَة، مِنْ فَضْلِكَ.
lines.en: Good evening! Where are you flying to today? Your passport and ticket, please.

lines.ar: مَسَاءُ النُّور. أُسَافِرُ إِلَى الْقَاهِرَة. تَفَضَّلْ، هٰذَا جَوَازُ سَفَرِي.
lines.en: Good evening. I'm flying to Cairo. Here you are, this is my passport.

lines.ar: شُكْرًا. ضَعْ حَقِيبَتَكَ عَلَى الْمِيزَان، لَوْ سَمَحْتَ… وَزْنُهَا ثَلَاثُونَ كِيلُو!
lines.en: Thank you. Put your suitcase on the scales, please… It weighs thirty kilos!
segs: your bag, your suitcase (to a man)

lines.ar: ثَلَاثُونَ؟! هَلْ هٰذَا أَكْثَرُ مِنَ الْمَسْمُوح؟ فِيهَا هَدَايَا كَثِيرَة لِأَصْدِقَائِي فِي الْقَاهِرَة.
lines.en: Thirty?! Is that more than is allowed? There are lots of presents in it for my friends in Cairo.

lines.ar: نَعَم، الْمَسْمُوح ثَلَاثَة وَعِشْرُونَ كِيلُو فَقَطْ. يَجِبُ أَنْ تَدْفَعَ عَنْ كُلِّ كِيلُو زِيَادَة.
lines.en: Yes, the limit is only twenty-three kilos. You have to pay for every extra kilo.

lines.ar: كَمْ أَدْفَعُ؟ وَهَلْ مِنَ الْمُمْكِن أَنْ آخُذَ بَعْضَ الْأَشْيَاء مَعِي فِي حَقِيبَةِ الْيَد؟
lines.en: How much do I pay? And is it possible to take some things with me in my hand luggage?

lines.ar: مُمْكِن. حَقِيبَةُ الْيَد حَتَّى سَبْعَة كِيلُو. أَوْ تَدْفَعُ عَشَرَةَ دَنَانِير عَنْ كُلِّ كِيلُو.
lines.en: It's possible. Hand luggage can be up to seven kilos. Or you pay ten dinars for every kilo.

lines.ar: عَشَرَةُ دَنَانِير لِكُلِّ كِيلُو؟ هٰذَا أَغْلَى مِنَ الْهَدَايَا! لَحْظَة، مِنْ فَضْلِكَ.
lines.en: Ten dinars a kilo? That's more expensive than the presents! One moment, please.

lines.ar: أَخَذْتُ الْكُتُب وَالْكُوفِيَّة مِنَ الْحَقِيبَة. هَلْ وَزْنُهَا الْآنَ أَقَلُّ؟
lines.en: I've taken the books and the keffiyeh out of the suitcase. Does it weigh less now?

lines.ar: نَعَم، الْآنَ ثَلَاثَة وَعِشْرُونَ كِيلُو بِالضَّبْط. مُمْتَاز! تَفَضَّلْ، هٰذِهِ بِطَاقَةُ الصُّعُود.
lines.en: Yes, now it's exactly twenty-three kilos. Excellent! Here you are, this is your boarding pass.

lines.ar: شُكْرًا جَزِيلًا! مِنْ أَيِّ بَوَّابَة تُغَادِرُ الطَّائِرَة، وَمَتَى يَجِبُ أَنْ أَكُونَ هُنَاكَ؟
lines.en: Thank you very much! Which gate does the plane leave from, and when do I have to be there?

lines.ar: مِنَ الْبَوَّابَة رَقْم ثَلَاثَة، فِي السَّاعَة السَّابِعَة. رِحْلَة سَعِيدَة، وَلَا تَشْتَرِ هَدَايَا أُخْرَى!
lines.en: From gate number three, at seven o'clock. Have a good flight, and don't buy any more presents!

mistakes.wrong: عَشَرَةُ دَنَانِير لِكُلِّ كِيلُو؟ هٰذَا غَالٍ مِنَ الْهَدَايَا!
mistakes.right: عَشَرَةُ دَنَانِير لِكُلِّ كِيلُو؟ هٰذَا أَغْلَى مِنَ الْهَدَايَا!
mistakes.why: 'More expensive than' is aghlā min; ghālin min does not compare.

mistakes.wrong: هَلْ مِنَ الْمُمْكِن أَنْ آخُذُ بَعْضَ الْأَشْيَاء؟
mistakes.right: هَلْ مِنَ الْمُمْكِن أَنْ آخُذَ بَعْضَ الْأَشْيَاء؟
mistakes.why: After an the verb ends in -a: an ākhudha.

title: At the hotel reception
intro: Daniel arrives at a small hotel near Petra and soon has to go back to the reception desk. Useful phrases: لَوْ سَمَحْتِ (excuse me, to a woman), عِنْدِي مُشْكِلَة (I have a problem) and أَرْجُو أَنْ… (please…).

dialogue.title: A room that is too hot
dialogue.culture: Small hotels in Wadi Musa are often family businesses, and the receptionist is happy to help with taxis, restaurants and tickets for Petra. If something in your room does not work, go to the desk and say politely لَوْ سَمَحْتِ، عِنْدِي مُشْكِلَة.

lines.ar: مَسَاءُ الْخَيْر، وَأَهْلًا بِكُمْ فِي فُنْدُقِ الْوَادِي! هَلْ عِنْدَكُمْ حَجْز؟
lines.en: Good evening, and welcome to the Valley Hotel! Do you have a booking?

lines.ar: مَسَاءُ النُّور. نَعَم، الْحَجْز بِاسْمِ لَيْلَى: غُرْفَتَانِ لِلَيْلَةِ السَّبْت.
lines.en: Good evening. Yes, the booking is in Layla's name: two rooms for Saturday night.

lines.ar: أَهْلًا! أَنْتُمْ أَصْدِقَاءُ لَيْلَى. تَفَضَّلْ، هٰذَا مِفْتَاحُ الْغُرْفَة الْكَبِيرَة، رَقْم مِئَة وَعَشَرَة، فِي الطَّابِق الْأَوَّل.
lines.en: Welcome! You're Layla's friends. Here you are, this is the key to the big room, number one hundred and ten, on the first floor.

lines.ar: لَوْ سَمَحْتِ، عِنْدِي مُشْكِلَة. الْمُكَيِّف فِي الْغُرْفَة لَا يَعْمَلُ، وَالْغُرْفَة حَارَّة جِدًّا.
lines.en: Excuse me, I have a problem. The air conditioning in the room doesn't work, and the room is very hot.

lines.ar: آسِفَة جِدًّا! هَلْ تُرِيدُ غُرْفَة أُخْرَى؟ عِنْدَنَا غُرْفَة أَكْبَرُ وَأَهْدَأُ فِي الطَّابِق الثَّانِي.
lines.en: I'm very sorry! Would you like another room? We have a bigger, quieter room on the second floor.

lines.ar: نَعَم، مِنْ فَضْلِكِ. هَلْ مِنَ الْمُمْكِن أَنْ أَرَاهَا أَوَّلًا؟
lines.en: Yes, please. Is it possible to see it first?

lines.ar: طَبْعًا. تَفَضَّلْ، هٰذَا مِفْتَاحُ الْغُرْفَة رَقْم خَمْسَة فِي الطَّابِق الثَّانِي. الْمِصْعَد عَلَى الْيَسَار.
lines.en: Of course. Here you are, this is the key to room number five on the second floor. The lift is on the left.

lines.ar: الْغُرْفَة الْجَدِيدَة أَفْضَلُ بِكَثِير، وَالْمُكَيِّف يَعْمَلُ. شُكْرًا! سُؤَال آخَر: أَيْنَ نَأْكُلُ الْعَشَاء؟
lines.en: The new room is much better, and the air conditioning works. Thank you! Another question: where can we have dinner?

lines.ar: مَطْعَمُ الْفُنْدُق مَفْتُوح حَتَّى السَّاعَة الْعَاشِرَة، وَهُوَ أَرْخَصُ مِنْ مَطَاعِمِ الْمَدِينَة.
lines.en: The hotel restaurant is open until ten o'clock, and it's cheaper than the restaurants in town.

lines.ar: مُمْتَاز. وَأَرْجُو أَنْ تَطْلُبِي لَنَا تَاكْسِي غَدًا فِي السَّاعَة السَّادِسَة وَالنِّصْف إِلَى مَدْخَلِ الْبَتْرَاء.
lines.en: Excellent. And please order us a taxi tomorrow at half past six to the entrance of Petra.
segs: you order (to a woman, after an)

lines.ar: بِكُلِّ سُرُور. التَّاكْسِي يَنْتَظِرُكُمْ أَمَامَ الْفُنْدُق، وَالْفُطُور يَبْدَأُ فِي السَّاعَة السَّادِسَة.
lines.en: With pleasure. The taxi will wait for you in front of the hotel, and breakfast starts at six o'clock.
segs: it waits for you (to several people)

lines.ar: شُكْرًا جَزِيلًا عَلَى الْمُسَاعَدَة! تُصْبِحِينَ عَلَى خَيْر.
lines.en: Thank you very much for your help! Good night.

mistakes.why: Salma is a woman, so say law samaḥti.
The comparative never changes for a feminine word: afḍal.
